title: South Korea plans to move its anti-piracy unit closer to the Strait of Hormuz
note: South Korea's defence ministry will ask parliament to widen the operating area of its Cheonghae anti-piracy unit to about 650 km from the strait, and Yonhap reports mine-clearing assets will be added. The move follows US pressure for support in the Iran war and ties Seoul more closely to Gulf security.

title: US sanctions Indian and Turkish firms accused of helping Iran's shadow fleet
note: The US Treasury says a network sold fraudulent ship registries, including for Guyana and Laos, to Iranian tankers, and a Turkey-based company serviced sanctioned Iranian airlines. The State Department frames the action as cutting revenue the Iranian government uses to fund its activities.
limitations: The accusations come from US authorities and the targeted parties have not been heard in this report. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: UK MPs find the country dangerously reliant on China for critical minerals
note: A parliamentary committee says the UK depends heavily on China for raw materials used in defence, renewable energy and AI. It calls for a central policy and a critical minerals finance facility to fund mines and diversification.
limitations: The findings are committee recommendations and the government has not committed to act on them. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: UN refugee chief says more than 117 million people are forcibly displaced
note: The UN refugee agency head told a General Assembly committee that conflict, violence and persecution have forced over 117 million people from their homes. Dwindling humanitarian funding is straining aid to displaced people and host countries.
limitations: The figure is a global aggregate from the UN and the briefing does not break it down by conflict. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: Ukraine and partners coordinate in Brussels ahead of Abu Dhabi talks with Russia
note: The European Commission hosted representatives of the US, Ukraine, NATO and several European countries to coordinate efforts to end the war. A US-convened round with Ukrainian and Russian delegations in Abu Dhabi is due within about a week.
limitations: Coordination meetings do not show that Russia is ready to accept terms or that a ceasefire will follow. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: US midterm results shift the politics of the Iran, Gaza and Ukraine wars
note: Al Jazeera reports the governing party lost heavily, with economic worry over oil prices and tariffs a factor, but Democrats lack the two-thirds majority needed to override a presidential veto. The result changes domestic pressure on US war policy without removing the president's authority.
